ISSUE-FIXER Step 0.5 — registry lookup and ISS file creation for GH-681 (ISS-0659).

The issue is well-documented in the GitHub body. 31 integration test files bypass TestHarness's advisory lock (PR #494's fix scope) and remain racy under the full test-integration suite. Evidence: sch303_timer_dlq_test.zig, spt01_iss0068_onboarding_schema_test.zig, iss0185_dual_schema_test.zig, env01_test.zig, env05_test.zig all share the same root cause — they manage their own db.Pool directly and never call TestHarness.init()/deinit(), so PR #494's serialization has no effect on them.

1. Search docs/issues/ for an existing entry that already references github_issue=https://github.com/tvolodi/R-Co/issues/681. If found, link to it.
2. If no entry exists: create docs/issues/ISS-0659.json with status=IN_PROGRESS, severity=MAJOR, github_issue=https://github.com/tvolodi/R-Co/issues/681. Include the 5 root-cause failure files, the 31 affected files list, and the two fix options (a) extend advisory lock to all 31 files, or (b) scope resetTestData() to per-tenant/per-fixture.
3. Verify the local ID ISS-0659 is not already in use.
4. Record a Step 1 diagnosis summary in the handoff result pointing to PR #494 as the prior fix, with explicit 'this issue documents the boundary of PR #494's fix scope' framing.
acceptance_criteria: Step 1 root cause diagnosis is recorded in handoff.result.summary
No duplicate github_issue field across docs/issues/*.json

result.summary: Step 0.5 registry lookup complete. ISS-0659 already exists at docs/issues/ISS-0659.json (created 2026-08-10T17:10:58Z by the WF03-GH679-20260810 run that root-caused this issue); the entry already references github_issue=https://github.com/tvolodi/R-Co/issues/681 and contains all required fields (5 root-cause failure files sch303/spt01/iss0185/env01/env05, 31-file TestHarness-bypass list, evidence_run clean-reset control, two fix options (a/b), prevention). No duplicate github_issue found across docs/issues/*.json (grep returned exactly 1 hit, the existing ISS-0659 entry). Linked the existing entry to this run by flipping status OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS, setting handoff_id=a6810000-...-0050, stamping last_updated=2026-08-10T17:25:13Z, and updating run_id to WF03-GH681-20260810 (was WF03-GH679-20260810 from when the entry was originally filed). Step 1 diagnosis (handover to CODE-DESIGNER Step 2): root cause is precisely documented in the GitHub issue body and in the ISS-0659 root_cause field -- PR #494 (merged prior to this run, closing GH-486/ISS-0162) fixed cross-binary races by having TestHarness hold an advisory lock for its full lifetime; that fix is TestHarness-to-TestHarness ONLY. 31 integration test files (identified by grep tests/integration/*.zig for direct db.Pool.init usage without TestHarness) bypass that lock and remain racy. This issue documents the BOUNDARY of PR #494's fix scope, not a new defect. The design question for CODE-DESIGNER is which of the two fix options to take: (a) extend the advisory-lock pattern to every self-managed-pool binary (lower-risk, reuses verified mechanism, but is a per-file retrofit), or (b) scope resetTestData()'s DELETEs and any ad-hoc schema-provisioning calls to per-tenant/per-fixture (more invasive, touches resetTestData() itself, closes the gap for future new test files too). The 3 allocator-leak failures observed in the same control run (api03_instance_read_test, adp06_pipeline_run_correlation_test, sim01_04_simulation_mode_test) are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here (different symptom class, not diagnosed) -- file separately if pursued. The iss105_token_model_test failure is also out of scope (already fixed in WF03-GH679-20260810). Acceptance: rerun the clean-reset control (fresh db_test volume + fresh zig build migrate + single zig build test-integration invocation) and confirm the 5 non-leak failures do not reproduce across 3+ consecutive clean runs.
